name: _sparse_log_softmax
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_log_softmax(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract — all overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation — and must not be narrowed to this one signature; no tests are removed or reference behavior adapted to fit it. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::_sparse_log_softmax.Dimname(Tensor self, str dim, *, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor; aten::_sparse_log_softmax.int(Tensor self, int dim, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor; aten::_sparse_log_softmax.out(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); aten::_sparse_log_softmax(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float) -> Tensor. Semantics derived from the tests: computes log_softmax over a sparse COO tensor. For dim >= sparse_dim each stored value block is normalized over its dense axis; for dim < sparse_dim the entries sharing the other sparse coordinates are pooled over the last sparse axis. The native kernel coalesces uncoalesced COO inputs internally, so the output holds one entry per distinct coordinate, and the backward test computes gradients with respect to the sparse input and compares them against the reference. Out-of-range dim (including every dim of a rank-0 sparse COO tensor) raises IndexError. Only float32/float64 have a kernel for the .default form; the RuntimeError rejections for other input dtypes (bfloat16, float16, float8_e4m3fn, float8_e5m2, bool, int8, uint8, int32, int64), for the .int dtype= parameter (int64, bfloat16, float16) and for half_to_float=True are collected only for the measured nvidia vendor, with the rejection wording measured on that backend, and are not claimed for other backends. A strided (dense) input raises RuntimeError from the tested candidate, while the pytest comment records that the native operator raises NotImplementedError (a RuntimeError subclass). The .int overload carries an optional ScalarType? dtype conversion parameter and the .Dimname overload takes a str dim; the .out overload writes into Tensor(a!) out, mutates it and returns it aliased. Those overload-dependent behaviors and errors remain owned by the pytest.
